bull_bear.body:
Consolidated net worth ₹2,655 cr as of 31-Mar-2026, cited as the buffer for both prop-desk capital needs
(post RBI circular) and continued MTF book growth; capital is being actively deployed into the retail
franchise (MTF funding, new branches) rather than returned to shareholders — no buyback/dividend commentary
on this call.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- RBI circular (eff. 1-Jul-2026) curbing bank guarantees/intraday limits for proprietary trading — ~20%
  estimated impact on prop-side deposits/limits; SEBI liquidity-provider/market-maker framework (which could
  restore guarantee eligibility for prop/arbitrage desks) still 3-4 months from being framed.
- High transaction/compliance costs and frequent regulatory change cited as structural industry headwinds
  (generic, not company-specific — no listed beneficiary mapped).
- MTF growth explicitly market-dependent — mgmt declines to guarantee the ₹650cr FY27 target if sentiment
  turns; India cited by mgmt as the weakest-performing major Asian market over the past year.
- Consolidated PAT decline YoY (FY26 vs FY25) on fair-value marks — watch whether this reverses or recurs.
- Internal inconsistency in stated standalone FY26 revenue figure (₹395cr) vs stated Q4 standalone revenue
  (₹383cr) — needs clarification next quarter/filing.
- uTrade multi-broker expansion stalled by SEBI vendor-infrastructure circular — a revenue-diversification
  initiative now delayed indefinitely.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
Confident, growth-oriented tone; management proactively addressed two analyst pushbacks (Q4 margin
seasonality, MTF funding-cost optics) with specific numbers rather than deflecting. Took an analyst's
suggestion (region-wise branch revenue disclosure) as an action item ("point noted, will do") — a small
positive governance/responsiveness signal. Management was also candid that the standalone/consolidated PAT
divergence was driven by non-operating fair-value marks rather than claiming pure operating strength across
the board.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The RBI circular is explicitly framed by management as pushing all "hybrid" brokers (client + prop) toward
  converting intraday facilities into bank guarantees tied to the client book — a structural incentive for
  full-service brokers to grow retail/client-side business specifically to preserve prop-desk funding access.
- Company frames itself as wanting to become "a Zerodha moment for algo trading" via uTrade over a 5-year
  horizon — an ambitious, unquantified aspiration flagged for tracking, not yet supported by revenue disclosure
  (mgmt explicitly said "revenue is not the focus" for uTrade currently).
- Client-side trading turnover crossing prop-side turnover for the first time (>53% vs 47%) is a genuine
  inflection point in the business mix, independent of the RBI regulatory driver.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "The Board of Directors declared the first interim dividend of INR 0.50 per equity share of face value INR 2 each."
- Debt to Equity of 0.23x (FY24), 0.21x (FY25), 0.25x (FY26); Net Worth INR 17,468 Mn (FY24), INR 23,340 Mn (FY25), INR 26,350 Mn (FY26).
- Balance sheet is liquidity-heavy: Other Bank Balances grew INR 15,613 Mn (FY24) to INR 19,147 Mn (FY25) to INR 26,070 Mn (FY26), alongside Cash and Cash Equivalents of INR 5,228 Mn in FY26; Loans grew INR 3,416 Mn to INR 5,261 Mn to INR 7,117 Mn over FY24-FY26.
- Funding mix shifted: Debt Securities went from nil (FY24) to INR 301 Mn (FY25) to INR 1,433 Mn (FY26), with Borrowings (other than debt securities) at INR 3,869 / 4,564 / 5,278 Mn over the same years.
- Shareholding as on 30 June 2026: Promoter 48.62%, Public 49.02%, FPI 1.88%, DII 0.48%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Standalone vs consolidated gap**: consolidated Q4/FY26 profitability trails standalone due to fair-value marks
  on investments held by group companies plus weaker market conditions at the group level.
- **Prop trading**: ~70% of revenue but only ~49% (consolidated) / ~52% (standalone) of FY26 profitability;
  client-side turnover crossed >53% for the first time (vs 47% prop) — mgmt frames this as a structural shift.
- **ADTO detail (Q4 FY26)**: options ~18% of quarterly ADTO; commodity ADTO reported as jumping sharply
  YoY (mgmt cited "~14 billion" in the year-ago quarter rising to "~4,500-5,000" in Q4 FY26 — units/scale as
  stated on the call, ambiguous, not independently reconciled); cash-market ADTO up from ~₹1,500 cr to ~₹2,000
  cr Q4-on-Q4.
- **NBFC/MTF book**: NIM of 17.64% for FY26, ~flat vs FY25; mgmt says NIM will likely trend down as the book
  is grown more conservatively (secured lending, lower leverage vs FY23/FY24 levels).
- **uTrade**: flagship algo-trading platform; multi-broker expansion (talks with Motilal Oswal, Dhan and others)
  stalled by a new SEBI circular requiring third-party trading-tech vendors to set up separate infrastructure
  per broker — cost-prohibitive at current scale; Share India (as the originating broker) continues to push
  uTrade to its own retail base instead.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Hybrid-broker classification (meaningful client-side turnover >53%) qualifies Share India for bank guarantees
  on the client book even as RBI curbs guarantees/intraday limits for pure proprietary trading — a real,
  call-evidenced regulatory-arbitrage advantage over prop-only peers as of the 1-Jul-2026 RBI circular.
- Tier-3 direct-branch model: removes sub-broker/mediator margin, letting Share India charge better MTF interest
  spreads in under-served geographies (mgmt cites Hyderabad performing ahead of an earlier Calcutta branch).

business.body:
- "Share India Securities Ltd was founded in 1994 and is headquartered in Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India"; described as "A 31-year young, technology-driven financial services leader, recognised for strong capabilities in Algorithmic Trading and advanced Fintech solutions" with "Trust of 31+ Years".
- The deck's central thesis is "A Structural Shift in Business Quality" from Traditional Broker to Fintech Platform: manual/dealer-driven to "Algorithmic & API-driven"; transaction-dependent revenue to "Platform + subscription + interest-led revenue"; limited IP to "Proprietary strategies, models & tech"; volume cyclicality to "Higher recurring & annuity income"; "Client = Trader" to "Client = Platform user".
- "Operates a pan-India distribution network with 225 branches and franchises across 19 states and UTs", with a comprehensive service portfolio across all branches: retail broking, margin trading facility, merchant banking, lending solutions, mutual fund distribution, insurance distribution and portfolio management services.
- Proprietary tech stack is the claimed moat: "Proprietary platforms uTrade Algos and Algowire Trading Technologies deliver AI and ML driven algorithmic strategies", with Algowire providing "latency-optimized, institutional-grade trading infrastructure" that "Powers the proprietary trading desk and client-facing algo platforms", and Silverleaf Securities Research acting as "the quantitative research and strategy development arm for systematic trading" owning "the end-to-end lifecycle from research and model development to live deployment and risk control".
- Group structure spans a standalone business (prop trading, broking in equity/F&O/commodities, MF distribution, research, depository participant) plus subsidiaries covering insurance broking, NBFC, investment banking, algo platform, IFSC/global equity trading entities, asset management and a digital investment distribution platform.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [NBFC asset quality] Deck states GNPA 4.05%, NNPA 2.26%, NIM 4.44% and ROA 1.71% as of Q1-FY27 (ROA figures noted as "not annualized"); GNPA trend 4.82% / 2.58% / 4.87% / 4.30% / 4.05% and NNPA 3.30% / 1.49% / 2.98% / 2.66% / 2.26% across Q1-FY26 to Q1-FY27 - i.e. non-monotonic, with a sharp dip and rebound in the middle quarters.
- [Loan book vs AUM labels] The NBFC page labels INR 2,682 Mn as both "Loan Book" and "AUM"; AUM trend 3,014 / 2,534 / 2,470 / 2,653 / 2,682 (INR Mn) with disbursements 1,205 / 565 / 599 / 995 / 799 across Q1-FY26 to Q1-FY27 - AUM in Q1-FY27 is still below the Q1-FY26 level.
- [Investor relations] The presentation was "prepared by Valorem Advisors", an independent investor relations management service company, which disclaims responsibility for accuracy and completeness.
- [Marketing] "Participated across 4 awareness events during the quarter" - Wealth Expo 2026 (Hyderabad), Finbridge Event 2026 (Mumbai), JITO Wealth Expo (Surat) and BOTS (Bangalore).
- [Claim to note] The at-a-glance page asserts "Approved Strategies with 100% Accuracy: 20" - an unqualified accuracy claim the deck does not define or substantiate anywhere else.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
Q4 margin compression (both FY25 and FY26) attributed to seasonal/geopolitical market volatility, not a
structural March-quarter pattern per mgmt; full-year guidance of ~38% EBITDA / ~22% PAT margin (+/-2%)
reaffirmed. MTF funding cost currently elevated because FY26-end borrowings will accrue interest for a full
year only in FY27; mgmt is working on cheaper NCD/third-party borrowing lines to compress spread over time.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** Standalone PAT +368% YoY on a weak base; consolidated PAT roughly flat/-1% YoY on
  fair-value marks on group investments. MTF book ₹424cr (FY27 target ₹650cr). Client turnover crossed prop
  turnover for first time (>53%/47%). RBI prop-desk bank-guarantee/intraday-limit circular effective 1-Jul-2026
  — ~20% estimated impact on prop deposits/limits, cushioned by "hybrid broker" classification. uTrade crossed
  5,231 clients but multi-broker plan stalled by a new SEBI vendor-infrastructure circular. PMS AUM >₹100cr
  (FY27 target ₹200cr); AIF CAT-3 pending SEBI approval (targeted Q2 FY27); Share India Cred (debt arranging)
  launched, 6 issues closed, target ₹500cr by FY27; Silverleaf HFT merger still pending NCLT approval.
- _Q1 FY27 → check: actual RBI-circular bottom-line impact (mgmt guided "minimal"); MTF book trajectory
  (₹650cr FY27 target vs market conditions); PMS AUM progress toward ₹200cr; AIF CAT-3 SEBI approval status;
  Wealth Management 3rd-party distribution launch (targeted Q3); resolution of the standalone FY26 revenue
  figure inconsistency flagged in §2; Silverleaf NCLT merger status; whether client-turnover share continues
  climbing toward the 60% target._

outlook.body:
- Margin guidance (reaffirmed, annual basis): EBITDA margin ~38% (+/-2%); PAT margin ~22% (+/-2%) — mgmt says Q4 dips (seen in both FY25 and FY26) are geopolitical-volatility driven, not structural, and should not recur every year.
- MTF book target: ₹650 cr by FY27 (from ₹424cr FY26-end), contingent on "normal" market conditions — mgmt explicitly caveats this is not assured; low-single-digit downside deviation possible if sentiment sours.
- PMS AUM target: ₹200 cr by FY27-end (from >₹100cr already raised in the PMS's first quarter).
- Revenue-mix target: client-side turnover to reach ~60% (from >53% now) and client-side profitability to >50-55% (from ~49-52% consolidated / ~52% standalone) by FY26-end/FY27; 3-year aspirational goal is 70% client / 30% prop (vs current ~49-52% prop contribution to PAT).
- AIF (CAT-3) launch: SEBI approval expected end of Q2 (FY27), operations targeted to start within FY27.
- Wealth Management (3rd-party product distribution, under Charu Sehgal): operations to start Q3 (of FY27, per hiring timeline referenced on the call).
- Branch build-out: 7 Tier-3 branches already live (Hyderabad, Indore, Bhopal, Varanasi, Agra, Raipur, Nagpur); 6 more targeted by FY-end; long-term goal of 30 ground branches over the next 2-3 years, each targeted at ₹10-15cr MTF/year.
- Share India Cred (debt arranging): target ≥₹500 cr worth of NCD issuances by FY27 (6 issues closed so far since Q1 FY27 start).
- Silverleaf HFT merger: NCLT approval pending, mgmt expects resolution "in a maximum [of a couple of] quarters" (imprecise wording on the call).
- RBI prop-desk bank-guarantee/intraday-limit curb effective 1-Jul-2026: mgmt estimates ~20% reduction in overall deposits/limits used on the prop side but expects minimal bottom-line impact (per-trade margins should widen as ~₹40,000-50,000 cr of capital is estimated to exit the market industry-wide); existing bank guarantees continue until expiry — stated once as "up to 30th June" and separately as "by up to March 2027" (two different sounding dates given on the same call — verbatim, not reconciled).

deepdive.thesis:
Standalone Q4 beat sharply on a weak base (PAT +368% YoY) while consolidated FY26 PAT was flat-to-down YoY on
fair-value marks on group investments, not the operating business; the real story is a multi-year diversification
push (MTF, PMS/AIF, Wealth, debt issuance via Share India Cred, uTrade algo platform, Tier-3 branch build-out) to
cut reliance on the ~49-52% profit contribution from proprietary trading, just as a new RBI circular (effective
1-Jul-2026) curbs bank funding support for prop-desk intraday trading.
